thread.title: Apple Watchers Are Already Looking Toward the Next Next iPhones

title: Apple Watchers Are Already Looking Toward the Next Next iPhones
text:
Apple Watchers Are Already Looking Toward the Next Next iPhones By Jan. 11, 2019 12:18 p.m. ET Order Reprints Text size
Forget about the 2018 iPhones. It’s all about the 2020s now.
As Apple (AAPL) and its investors continue to digest the substance of the company’s revelations about slowing sales in China and ponder what it says about its hardware business and the crucial iPhone—just as it scales back on the data it provides on phone sales—attention is starting to move past the last round of new devices, past the next round, to the round after that.
CEO Tim Cook used a TV interview earlier this week to try to reassure investors—and, surely, consumers—that there is “a culture of innovation in Apple.” For millions, that still means physical products that make others seem insufficient, and a Friday Wall Street Journal article, citing “people familiar with the matter,” hinted at what they might expect . (Some of the Apple news out of this week’s CES trade show , meanwhile, offered a glimpse at where its service offerings may be headed .)
Read more: Why There’s Still Plenty of Value in Apple’s Core
The Journal reported that three more new iPhones are due this fall that could include upgraded cameras that bring them better in line with some competitors’ products. Samsung Electronics (005930.Korea), for example, has a four-rear-camera phone meant to give more tools for telephoto and wide-angle shooters, as well as those who need “normal” lenses. Apple’s three-camera phone would be its first.
And in 2020, the Journal wrote, the company’s entire lineup could have organic light-emitting diode, or OLED, displays, which are considered a step up from liquid crystal displays. Apple kept an LCD on its new model XR , which made the phone more affordable than its other late-2018 phones. That hasn’t helped prop up sales as much as hoped.
Much more, however, is expected.
“We believe 2019 iPhone models are unlikely to involve significant upgrades” beyond those mentioned above, JPMorgan analyst Samik Chatterjee wrote Friday, citing “feedback” from Apple suppliers. Newsletter Sign-up
But “in 2020, we expect a more material refresh, including adoption of world-facing 3-D sensing”—which could give phones the power to record three-dimensional images or do advanced motion recognition, for example—”substantially greater support for augmented reality and virtual reality applications, inclusion of 5G modems, and a material change on display and casing form factor,” he wrote.
Apple didn’t immediately respond to an emailed request for comment on the Journal’s story and possible product changes in 2019 and 2020.
The company’s shares have fallen in 2019 as the S&P 500 has risen, though they’re up this week as of midday Friday. That’s a sign that investors think the company can work its way out of its roughly four-month slump. The latest news offers clues as to how that might happen.
